materialDissent: Packet framing: the round-13 working-tree diff SHA-256 is presented as 'closing the evidence chain'. As an evidence artifact inside a packet-only review it is self-attested — a reviewer with no tree access cannot recompute it, and `git diff` output is config-sensitive (diff.context/-U, core.autocrlf, textconv, diff.noprefix, color settings are not pinned in the command shown), so an auditor reproducing it on a differently-configured checkout could get a different hash without any content divergence. It is a useful audit aid for a future auditor on this machine, not independent proof of packet fidelity for this round. This does not change my approve decision; the code and tests stand on their own reading.
review.recommendation: Approve as-is and ship. The design is coherent and minimal: `youngestMarkerAgeMs` now returns a three-valued result (Infinity = no markers, null = unmeasurable, finite = measurable age), both call sites (verified by the fresh grep as the only two, lines 1120 and 1169) compare directly rather than doing arithmetic on the possibly-null value, and `gateExitCode()` centralizes the mapping so the three `fail(...)` sites in `unfreezeDraft`/`submitDraft`/`discardDraft` cannot drift apart. Exit 20 is strictly narrower than the old exit 2 behavior — it fires only for a completed zero-match search with a parseable, non-future marker below the floor; poll exhaustion, search failure, unmeasurable age, and submit's retry-verification wait all remain exit 2, and each of those branches has an explicit test. Code 20 is safely below the shell-reserved 126+ range and does not collide with 16–19, asserted by the updated inventory test. Documentation is consistent across three surfaces (spec accepted-addition note, JIRA_QUEUE.md, embedded `--help` prose), each including 20 in the dry-run list; the SKILL.md grep confirms no prose surface carries a stale inventory. Two optional, non-blocking follow-ups if a future round touches this code: (1) collapse the dual vocabulary noted in the strongest objection, and (2) if any non-Markdown consumer outside the CLI ever branches on exit 2 for this gate, record a grep for it once.
review.strongestObjection: Weighted low, non-blocking, maintainability rather than correctness: `VERIFICATION_REASON` now carries two different tokens for the same physical condition, and they are used in two different namespaces. The audit record for a below-floor measurable marker is written with `reason: MARKER_YOUNGER_THAN_INDEX_LAG_MINIMUM`, while the value returned to the caller for that same branch is `reason: VERIFICATION_REASON.INDEX_LAG` — and `gateExitCode()` matches only on `INDEX_LAG`. The other two gate returns (`SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE`, `MARKER_AGE_UNMEASURABLE`) reuse the audit vocabulary directly, so the object's `reason` field is a mix of audit reasons and one exit-code routing token. The failure mode is silent: a future edit that harmonizes the return to `MARKER_YOUNGER_THAN_INDEX_LAG_MINIMUM` (the obvious-looking cleanup, since it matches the audit line two lines above) would fall through `gateExitCode()` to `EXIT.STATE_ERROR` with no type error and no crash — caught only because `tests/jira-queue.test.mjs` asserts `EXIT.INDEX_LAG_BLOCKED` at the unfreeze, dry-run-submit, and discard sites. Test coverage makes this detectable, so it does not block; the cheap hardening if this file is edited again is a single derived mapping (e.g. exit code selected from the audit reason) rather than two parallel strings.
unresolvedQuestions: Consumer-side impact of the exit 2 -> 20 narrowing has been verified only for Markdown/prose surfaces. The round-13 greps cover `plugins/kstack --include="*.md"` and `plugins/kstack/skills/*/SKILL.md`; no grep was shown over non-Markdown consumers (other `.mjs` scripts, shell wrappers, git/Claude hooks, CI steps) for code that branches on exit status 2 from a `kstack-jira` unfreeze/submit/discard invocation. Such a consumer would now see 20 and could mis-classify it as success or as an unhandled failure. Residual risk is low — the packet's own spec context states skills are restricted to `draft`, which never reaches the pre-mutation gate — which is why this is recorded as a question rather than a failed check.
